thread:
maria-customer: Hey team — we rotated our service API key in Vault at 09:12 UTC and a subset of traffic (EU edge) started getting 401s ~2m later. Rolling key back doesn't immediately clear it. Can someone triage? Logs: https://s3.company.example/maria/rotation-logs.tar.gz :rotating_light:

sam-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you confirm which client(s) and whether they use our SDK or call the REST API directly? Any repro steps?

maria-customer: It's our webhooks consumer (internal) and direct REST calls from EU region. Repro: curl against /v1/generate with Authorization: Bearer <new-key> returns 401. Old key intermittently accepted for ~90s, then 401s too.

eli-eng: @sam-support @raj-ops ping — sounds like a propagation/caching/tokens issue. Can you paste a minimal curl and the 401 response body? Also which Vault method did you use to rotate (kv v2 write vs. dynamic creds)?

maria-customer: curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer NEW_KEY" https://api-eu.redwood.example/v1/models
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
{
  "error": "invalid_api_key",
  "message": "api key not recognized"
}
We rotated by writing a new value to k/v2 at secret/services/mesa/apikey and updated helm values with the new value, then restarted the deployment. Vault agent on the pod is configured to render to /etc/creds/apikey.

sam-support: Thanks. Two quick possibilities: 1) edge caches an auth lookup (TTL) and still using old mapping, 2) sidecar/agent didn't pick up new file or env var shadowing from helm values. Can you check the container's env and /etc/creds inside the pod?

maria-customer: Checked: pod shows env REDWOOD_API_KEY=OLD_KEY (from helm chart) but /etc/creds/apikey contains NEW_KEY. We see the pod restarted after deploy.

raj-ops: Ah — this matches a known race: if the app prefers env var over file, and helm rendered a deprecated chart value that set REDWOOD_API_KEY at pod creation, the process may read env first. Also some EU edge instances cache token validity for ~60–120s TTL. If your app reads env on start, it will keep the old value until env updates and process restart.

eli-eng: That explains the intermittent acceptance of the old key (~90s) then 401s. The flow: Vault write -> file updated by agent -> app still using env (OLD_KEY) -> edge validates against control-plane which now rejects OLD_KEY -> 401 bursts. Two vectors: env shadowing and edge cache.

sam-support: For immediate mitigation: 1) kill/restart the application process in the pod so it reads file value (or update deployment to remove legacy env), 2) trigger a soft purge on EU edge auth cache for the customer (raj can do), 3) as a fallback, re-add the old key as a short-lived alias in the control plane while we complete rollout.

raj-ops: I'm purging the auth cache for your tenant in eu-1 now. Give it 30s and retry. Also checking edge logs for stale mapping.

vault-bot: Vault rotation event recorded: secret/services/mesa/apikey - version 4 created by maria-customer at 2024-08-01T09:12:03Z. Lease TTL: n/a (kv).

maria-customer: Purge done — retry shows more success but still some 401s from a small subset of visitors.

eli-eng: Two diagnostic asks: 1) provide the app process logs showing the API key it read at startup (redact actual key), 2) capture edge auth debug for a failing request id (we can correlate). If you can reproduce with a single request id, paste it here.

maria-customer: Attaching excerpt: "[09:12:07] INFO read_creds: source=/etc/creds/apikey value=***REDACTED***" then later "[09:14:30] WARN auth_check failed for token=OLD***". Failing request id: req_eu_9b7a2c.

raj-ops: Found req_eu_9b7a2c in edge logs — it hit an older auth shard that still had the pre-rotation mapping cached. TTL was 75s and it didn't refresh before the control-plane changed mapping. We're seeing two independent caches (edge L1 + region L2) — both needed purge. I've purged both.

sam-support: Good catch. Operational fixes we should recommend to customers: - avoid baking API keys into helm-value envs; prefer file + sidecar or use dynamic Vault tokens, - when rotating, coordinate a staged restart (or send SIGHUP) to processes that prefer envs, - include a short overlap window and aliasing in control plane for critical rotations.

eli-eng: Action items for Redwood platform: 1) Make edge auth cache TTL metadata visible per-tenant so SRE/support can judge purge needs, 2) add a short-lived alias feature to accept two key versions during rollouts, 3) update docs to call out helm-env shadowing and recommended Vault-agent render paths. I'll create GH issues.

oncall-engineer: Filing an incident-lite to track: INC-2024-813-rotation-cache. Assign to eng/runtime for alias support and docs.

maria-customer: Thanks all — after the second purge and a controlled pod restart the 401s stopped. Please keep me posted on alias feature. :thumbsup:

sam-support: Closing loop — we'll follow up with a postmortem and recommended runbook for rotation (link to draft will be posted here).

eli-eng: Draft GH issues: runtime#462 (alias-accept-two-versions), console#301 (expose-cache-ttl), docs#128 (rotation-helm-warning).

maria-customer: Appreciated. Logging the final confirmation: all clear at 09:25 UTC.

sam-support: Thanks, marking resolved. :white_check_mark:
